Subject: Lyra RFP: KMS/BYOK technical clarifications

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the materials so far. Our security team scanned the initial RFP submission and has a few clarifications that we need to include in the vendor evaluation pack. Could you confirm the following points and, if possible, attach any concise artifacts (diagram, attestation, runbook):

1) BYOK import workflow: Can you describe the end-to-end flow for importing customer wrapping keys? Specifically:
   - Supported transfer mechanisms (PKCS#12, PKCS#11, offline courier, etc.)
   - Whether the import key material ever leaves a customer-managed HSM boundary (i.e., support for offline-injected keys)
2) HSM attestation: Do you provide HSM vendor-signed attestation (e.g., CloudHSM / Thales / SafeNet) or a Redwood-signed operational attestation? Any example artifact would be helpful.
3) Remote export policy: Is there any scenario where key material can be exported in plaintext from your environment? If so, please enumerate controls.
4) Key rotation: What rotation modes do you support (automatic rollover with rewrap vs. manual rotate&re-encrypt)? Typical re-encryption window?
5) TLS and mTLS: For private deployments, does Redwood enforce TLS1.3 only? Do you support mutual TLS for service-to-service between customer ingress and the inference fleet?
6) Evidence: Please attach a short diagram showing key custody and a one-page playbook for emergency key revocation.

We need these details by EOD Mon 30 Aug so we can include them in our procurement packet.

Best,
Elaine
Elaine Zhou
Security Program Manager | Lyra Pharma

Hi Elaine — thanks for the clear list. Below are concise answers; I attached a short diagram and a 2‑page BYOK playbook for Lyra, plus a PDF summary tied to your RFP template.

Summary answers (short):
1) BYOK import workflow
   - Supported transfer mechanisms: PKCS#11 over secure channel for live HSM integrations, PKCS#12 (encrypted archive) via SFTP for tape/import, and an offline manual injection process for Private (on-prem) deployments where a Redwood field engineer performs HSM initialization in customer-controlled environment.
   - Import boundary: For hosted Redwood, customer wrapping keys are supplied encrypted (envelope-wrapped) and are never stored plaintext in Redwood control plane. For Dedicated/Private deployments, keys can be injected directly into customer-managed HSMs (no export).
2) HSM attestation
   - We can provide vendor-signed attestation where supported (e.g., AWS CloudHSM attestation statement) and a standardized Redwood operational attestation that references HSM serials, firmware, and FIPS level. Example attestation template attached.
3) Remote export policy
   - Default: No plaintext export of customer wrapping keys from HSM-protected modules. Export in wrapped form is permitted for migration. Exceptional export requires a documented, signed request and is logged/audited; we route such requests through legal & security with dual-approval.
4) Key rotation
   - Modes: automatic key rollover (preferred) with background rewrap of stored DEKs, or manual rotation with customer-approved window. Re-encryption window configurable; typical safe default is 14 days to rewrap active ciphertexts, with older versions retained for 90 days for rollback and audit.
5) TLS and mTLS
   - We support TLS1.2 and TLS1.3 in hosted; TLS1.3 is enforced for Private deployments and for mTLS-enabled ingress. Mutual TLS is supported between customer ingress and inference nodes in Dedicated/Private modes; hosted endpoints use token-based auth over TLS1.3 and can be fronted by a customer-managed mTLS proxy if required.
6) Evidence and playbook
   - Attached: redwood-kms-diagram-v2.png (custody boundaries), rationale-byok-playbook.docx (2 pages), Lyra-RFP-Attachment-KMS-Responses.pdf (RFP-aligned answers). Also shared a folder with example attestation templates: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cLyra-KMS-Evidence

Deliverables we can provide for your procurement packet:
- Vendor HSM attestation (where available)
- Redwood operational attestation (signed PDF)
- Key custody diagram and step-by-step BYOK runbook
- Example rotation schedule and a sample audit log extract (redacted)

If you want we can also provide a short recorded readout (15–20m) for your security review team.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Marcus / Monica — looping you in for two quick confirmations:

1) HSM models & witness: For Private deployments we support Thales nShield (nshield500, nshield Connect), AWS CloudHSM (where customer has VPC access), and Entrust/WehnTrust managed modules on-prem via PKCS#11. We need to confirm whether we allow in-person witness of initialization for Lyra — my read: yes, for customer-hosted hardware we can coordinate witness; for AWS CloudHSM we can provide vendor attestation and logs but not a physical witness. Marcus — pls confirm or correct the list and wording.

2) Exceptional export template & SLA: We currently route export requests through Security and Legal with dual-approval; turnaround is typically 3–5 business days once the request packet is complete. Monica — can you attach the export-request template we use and the standard approval SLAs? If there are any policy caveats (insurance, escrow), flag them here.

I want to get a short schedule for rotation rewrap cadence (a couple bullets) to send to Tyler.

Thanks — I plan to send a consolidated note to Lyra by 10:15 so they can hit procurement timelines.

—Lauren

Hi Elaine / Tyler — follow-ups and attachments per your request. Apologies for the quick thread — trying to keep to your procurement window.

Attached / linked items (in Drive):
- redwood-kms-diagram-v2.png — custody boundaries & example flow for BYOK (hosted vs. private)

- Lyra-RFP-Attachment-KMS-Responses.pdf — answers inline with your RFP spreadsheet
- Attestation templates (sample): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cLyra-KMS-Evidence

Answers to follow-ups:
- Supported HSMs for private/on-prem witness: Thales nShield (nshield Connect/500), Entrust/SafeNet HSMs via PKCS#11. For customer-managed cloud HSMs (e.g., AWS CloudHSM) we can provide vendor attestation statements but cannot provide physical witness. For on-prem installations we accommodate witnessed initialization under customer site policies; Redwood engineer will be present and we require a short site access form.
- Exceptional export template & SLA: Template attached in the Drive folder (Export-Request-Template.docx). Approval timeline: typically 3–5 business days; export requires dual sign-off (Security + Legal) and a documented transport plan. Any export will be done in wrapped form unless Lyra explicitly approves plaintext export under escrow terms (we discourage and require additional controls).
- Rotation schedule (sample):
   * Day 0: New wrapping key generated in HSM (version v2) and attested.
   * Days 1–3: Background rolling rewrap job operates on cold storage snapshots; each worker rewraps a shard to limit blast radius.
   * Day 4–14: Remaining active objects rewrapped; monitoring alerts for failed rewraps and automatic retries.
   * Day 15: Old key marked deprecated; retained for 90 days for rollback before scheduled destruction.

We can also provide a short readout with Security (15–20 minutes). If that works, propose Tue 31 Aug 08:00–09:00 PT (I can add Marcus for HSM specifics).

Next steps I will take: send the Redwood operational attestation PDF (signed) via the drive link and create a DocuSign for the export-request template in case you end up using it.
